title: Multimodal STEM Analysis of Aluminum Alloy with Multiscale Precipitates
content: Aluminum alloys have many applications in the aerospace and automotive industries, which require lightweight structural components. Common alloying elements such as Cu, Si, Mg, Mn, Li, Zn and Zr can introduce precipitates that contribute to additional desirable properties such as age hardening [1, 2] and enhanced thermal stability [3]. This study’s goal was to investigate the precipitate structures within an aluminum alloy Al 2099 using a holistic selection of STEM and 4D-STEM measurements available within the workflow of TESCAN TENSOR.
